notes: brasildefato.com.br is WordPress; robots.txt (200) disallows only /wp-admin/ and /search/ and advertises /sitemap.xml and /sitemap.xml?lang=en. PROBES: /sitemap.xml (200) is a FLAT urlset of ~62 KB, mostly section and static pages plus articles; /wp-sitemap.xml 404; /sitemap_index.xml 404; /sitemap.xml?lang=en 200 same shape; the per-day archive /2026/10/11/ (200, title 'Dia: 11 de outubro de 2026') server-renders only a 12-slug block, the rest of the day is loaded by JS, so archives are useless as a primary route. WINNING ROUTE: the open WP REST API, /wp-json/wp/v2/posts?per_page=100&after=2026-09-25T00:00:00&before=2026-10-26T00:00:00&orderby=date&order=desc&_fields=date,link,type, status 200, 15 pages (14x100 + 4), ~44s end to end. Each item gives `date` in site-local time (UTC-3, e.g. date 2026-10-25T14:09:22 vs date_gmt 17:09:22) and `link` = /YYYY/MM/DD/slug/, so the listed date is the site's own publication date and matches the URL path date. 1404 unique URLs, every one of the 31 days covered: min 10 (2026-09-27, Sunday), max 93 (2026-10-04, election day), check dates 2026-09-30=60, 2026-10-10=23, 2026-10-20=50. CROSS-CHECKS: the 2026-10-11 date archive lists exactly the same 12 slugs the API returns for that day, so the API is complete for the news stream; 15 re-fetched articles (3 per date, 5 dates) all HTTP 200 with 3791-10387 characters of text and a page date equal to the listed date (one late-night 2026-09-25 post carries JSON-LD datePublished 2026-09-26, 1 day off, which the check tolerates). SCOPE DECISION: only the `post` type is used. The custom types /wp-json/wp/v2/{column,art,correspondente,documentario,especiais,podcast,projeto,tabloide} answer 200 but publish under /colunista/<name>/YYYY/MM/DD/, /artista/, /documentario/, /projeto/, /tabloide/ (no root-level date path), are opinion columns and multimedia/project pages rather than news articles, and some are short landing pages, so they are deliberately excluded. FALLBACKS in the script: for any day under 15 URLs it reads the /YYYY/MM/DD/ archive (date from the archive day, which is also the URL path date); if the API fails or more than 3 days stay thin it also walks /sitemap.xml, recursing into any sitemapindex. On the real run both fallbacks added nothing, which confirms the API path is sufficient. No 403/429/WAF was hit at 1 req/s through polite_fetch; no Wayback CDX needed.
